title: Stream segment anchoring and checksum protocol for lossless token accounting
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem summary:
We have recurring repros where streaming sessions that experience intermittent network reconnects, compressed frame batches, or midstream model handoffs result in divergent token counts between the serving ledger and the client-visible accounting. The divergence surface includes: (1) missing tokens when partial frames are dropped and later retransmitted, (2) double-counting on client resume when the client replays a last-ack chunk, and (3) skew introduced by different tokenizers used by client-side pretokenization vs server canonicalizer. These manifest as incorrect quotas, unexpected rate-limit throttles, or ghost charges.

Why it matters:
- Customers see billing surprises or quota exhaustion from unseen double-charges.
- Rate limiter state becomes inconsistent leading to spurious 429s or excessive throttling.
- Investigation is costly for SREs and Billing.

Goal:
Design and implement a robust protocol and server-side pipeline changes that guarantee lossless, idempotent token accounting for streaming sessions across reconnects, compressed batches, and model handoffs. Provide instrumentation and an audit path to reconcile discrepancies and run retroactive corrections where safe.
acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming sessions produce an immutable per-session "anchor log" that lets us reconstruct canonical token attribution for any contiguous time window.
- After implementing the protocol, run a 2-week canary: detected accounting drift between serving ledger and audit ledger must be <= 0.01% on sampled traffic (confidence interval 95%).
- Client-visible resume semantics must be idempotent: replaying the final acknowledged chunk must not increment billed tokens.
- System handles compressed frames and multipart frames: checksum mismatch triggers deterministic reassembly flow, not blind crediting.
- New metrics and dashboards are present: session_anchors_total, anchor_replays, anchor_mismatch_rate, retrospective_corrections_applied.
- Migration plan executed without customer-visible billing regressions during rollout window.
proposed_solution:
High level:
1) Per-stream anchor records: every N output tokens (configurable, default 64) the server writes a signed anchor record containing (session_id, stream_offset_tokens, prefix_hash, tokenizer_version, model_variant, kernel_profile, timestamp). Anchors are persisted in both the fast ledger (for SLO) and an append-only audit ledger (for reconciliation).
2) Chunk checksums: each frame/batch carries a compact checksum of the tokenized bytes and the anchor id it relates to. During reconnect, the client includes last-received-anchor-id and last-received-offset.
3) Resume handshake: on reconnect the server compares client-sent anchor id/offset against the audit ledger. If in-range and checksums match, server returns a deterministic resume token that is idempotent; if mismatch, server triggers reassembly or requests client to resend from prior consistent anchor.
4) Tokenizer canonicalization: server uses canonical tokenizer to compute authoritative token counts. Clients can send pretokenized lengths; these are used only for speculative flows and never for billing. Anchors include tokenizer_version to detect drift.
5) Retroactive corrections: a background job scans anchors vs fast-ledger and, when safe and with low risk (customer not actively editing session), emits correction transactions / credits. All corrections are recorded in audit ledger with triggers for manual review above thresholds.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Writing anchors every N tokens increases persistence IO; we batch anchor writes and can tune N per tier.
- Anchor signing (HMAC) prevents tampering but adds CPU. We offload signing to a lightweight service.
- Some latency increase for the first resume handshake; we mitigate via cached anchor window in edge proxies.
tech_decisions:
- Anchor frequency: default 64 tokens (benchmarked for <0.5% added write QPS on high-throughput pods).
- Checksum algorithm: BLAKE2b-128 truncated to 128 bits for a good collision/size tradeoff.
- Anchor store: append-only Dynamo-like store (existing audit ledger) with a small fast Redis cache for last-anchor lookups.
- Resume protocol: synchronous verification for adjacent anchors, async fallthrough for older anchors (trigger background reconciliation).
- Backfill policy: corrections older than 90 days are logged but not automatically credited unless customer impact flagged.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for anchor encoding/decoding and checksum verification.
- Integration tests: simulated reconnects with partial frames, duplicate replays, compressed batches; assert idempotent billing behavior.
- Fuzz tests: random frame drops and out-of-order delivery for 1M synthetic sessions to ensure no double-counts.
- Load test: measure anchor write amplification at 1x, 5x, 10x production QPS; verify latency SLOs.
- Canary: enable anchors for 2% traffic for 48h, then 20% for 72h, then 100% of a non-critical region for one week before full rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag anchors behind runtime-config for controlled rollout.
2) Deploy server-side anchor writer to canary fleet.
3) Deploy lightweight anchor cache in edge proxies.
4) Enable resume-handshake verification for canary traffic.
5) Monitor anchor_mismatch_rate and reconciliation alerts; abort on spike >0.1% for two consecutive hours.
6) Ramp to 100% after 7 days stable.
7) Deploy retrospective correction worker in passive mode (logs only) for 72h, then enable write corrections with conservative thresholds.
monitoring_and_alerting:
New metrics: session_anchors_written, anchor_write_failures, anchor_mismatch_rate, anchor_resume_rejects, retrospective_corrections_count, billing_corrections_sum_usd.
Dashboards: per-region anchor health, pod-level anchor latency percentiles, reconciliation backlog.
Alerts: P1 if anchor_write_failures > 0.05% sustained for 15m; P0 if retrospective_corrections_count spikes above 100/hr.
